Syurte Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Syurte, Ukraine

Not demolished. Presumably established in the 19th century, this cemetery existed by 1873 per its oldest gravestone, used until WWII. Jews are believed to have arrived in the first half of the 18th century; population reached 45 by 1830 and 319 (19%) by 1880, rising sharply to 1,099 by 1921 (Czechoslovak period). Jews earned livelihoods in trade and crafts, running about 60 businesses and 26 workshops, alongside seven factories and a bank; the community included a doctor, pharmacists, and various officials and clerks. Hungarian forces arrived March 1939; 150 area Jews were drafted into forced labor battalions by 1940, with others sent to the Eastern Front where most perished, though some joined the Czechoslovak army instead. Population reached 1,423 (17%) by 1941; families without Hungarian citizenship were expelled that August to Kamianets-Podilskyi and murdered. Over 1,000 remaining Syurte Jews were deported to Auschwitz on May 22, 1944. No Jews live in the town today.
